label: prf:beta-decay-transfer-matrix
title: Proof of beta decay transfer matrix
html:
Proof. Proof of beta decay transfer matrix

Proof. Write h = q - q^{-1}. Then:

T_{pp} = T(1, 0): entries [[h, 1], [1, 0]]

T_{nn} = T(1, -h): entries [[0, 1], [1, -h]]

T_{\mathrm{mix}} = T(1, -h/2): entries [[h/2, 1], [1, -h/2]]

The differences T_{\mathrm{mix}} - T_{nn} and T_{pp} - T_{\mathrm{mix}} both equal [[h/2, 0], [0, h/2]] = \frac{h}{2} \mathbb{I}. \square

Explicit entries at the substrate parameter q:

  \Delta_\beta(q_0) = 
  \tfrac{1}{2}(q_0 - q_0^{-1}) \mathbb{I}
   \approx 
  \begin{pmatrix}
    +0.1045 & 0 \\
    0 & +0.1045
  \end{pmatrix}

The decay formula

At generator \sigma_i (affected by the converting nucleon at position p), the transfer matrix product factors as:

  M_i^{\mathrm{par}}(q) = L_i(q) \cdot T_{\mathrm{par}}(q) \cdot R_i(q)

where L_i is the product of matrices to the left of the converting crossing (unchanged) and R_i to the right (unchanged). The daughter matrix product is:

  M_i^{\mathrm{dau}}(q) = L_i(q) \cdot (T_{\mathrm{par}}(q) + \Delta_\beta(q)) \cdot R_i(q)

The change in the transfer matrix product:

  \Delta M_i(q) = L_i(q) \cdot \Delta_\beta(q) \cdot R_i(q)

The change in the Markov-traced volume:

  \Delta \hat{V}_i(q)
  = 
  z \cdot (\Delta M_i)_{11} + (\Delta M_i)_{21}

The Q-value (transition energy) in eigenfunction-basis (log-ratio) form:

  \mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{\mathrm{B}}
  \;:=\;
  \ln \frac{P_{\mathrm{dau}}(q)}{P_{\mathrm{par}}(q)}
  \cdot \frac{E_0}{z}
  \;=\;
  \frac{E_0}{z} \,
  \sum_{i=0}^{p} \ln \frac{\hat{V}_i^{\mathrm{dau}}(q)}{\hat{V}_i^{\mathrm{par}}(q)},

where the sum runs only over generators affected by the converting nucleon (generators \sigma_i with i > p cancel exactly), z = 1/(\sqrt q + 1/\sqrt q) is the Markov–Jones parameter (Hecke–Skein normalization), and the 1/z factor is not a calibration knob — it is the normalization required to map the eigenfunction observable \ln V_{\mathrm{pp}}/V_{\mathrm{nn}} onto MeV.

Form B is not a separate observable from the NF-counit form \mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{\mathrm{A}} = |\Delta(\mathrm{net})| \cdot E_0 of prop:neutron-qvalue-symbolic; the two are basis-change equivalent at leading order, with the explicit bridge identity given in prop:q-beta-spectral-bridge:

  \mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{\mathrm{A}}
  \;=\;
  \mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{\mathrm{B}} \cdot \bigl(1 + \tfrac{(z - 1)\,h}{2} + O(h^2)\bigr).

Form B is the natural basis for N \geq 1 brane-tower truncation analysis (where it composes additively across generators); Form A is canonical at N = 0 free neutron (where the NF counit is a closed combinatorial datum).
